chapters.title: Questions about violence and God’s answer

parts.text: Habakkuk asks why God allows violence, injustice, and the paralysis of law to continue. The LORD answers that he is raising the Chaldeans, a fierce nation whose armies seize others’ homes and scoff at rulers and fortifications. Their swift conquests gather countless captives, yet they become guilty by crediting their power to their god.

The prophet then asks how the holy and eternal God can use people more wicked than those they devour. He compares their victims to helpless fish caught in a net. The conquerors worship the very means of their success and enrich themselves through slaughter. Habakkuk’s question remains whether they will be allowed to keep destroying nations without restraint.

chapters.title: The appointed vision and the fall of pride

parts.text: Habakkuk takes his watch to await God’s answer. The LORD tells him to write the vision plainly and wait for its appointed fulfillment, which will certainly come. The proud soul is not upright, but the just shall live by his faith. The arrogant conqueror’s hunger for nations is as insatiable as death.

A series of woes announces repayment for plunder, unjust gain, bloodshed, degrading others, and trusting lifeless idols. Those exploited will rise against their oppressor, and even a house built by wrongdoing testifies against its owner. Glory will become shame, while the earth will be filled with knowledge of the LORD’s glory. Unlike silent manufactured gods, the LORD reigns in his holy temple, calling the earth to silence.

Habakkuk asks the LORD to renew his work and remember mercy in wrath. His prayer depicts God coming in brilliant majesty, shaking mountains and nations, commanding waters and heavenly lights, and marching to save his people. Images of divine warfare describe the overthrow of the wicked and God’s power over creation.

The vision leaves Habakkuk trembling as he awaits the day of trouble. Yet his final resolve does not depend on prosperity: even if figs, grapes, olives, grain, flocks, and herds all fail, he will rejoice in the LORD. The God of his salvation remains his strength, making his feet sure like a deer’s and enabling him to walk on the heights.
